text:
Marta: Morning — quick sync. We're doing a sunrise staging check-in for the model catalog launch. Need final entitlements/legal sign-off + perf owner confirmation for three open models (zephyr-3b, amber7b, nova-instruct). Can owners confirm status? Link to checklist: https://redwood.internal/docs/model-catalog/staging-checklist

Vikram: I own zephyr-3b perf. Baseline looks good but hitting a p99 tail on long-context runs (~2k tokens). There's a kernel selection PR in review: https://git.redwood/infra/zephyr-perf/pull/42 — ETA EOD for fixes.

Jess: Amber7b popped a licensing flag in the intake report — opened ticket CR-412. @olivia-legal can you confirm whether the model license + attribution we have is acceptable for hosted?

Olivia-Legal: On it. Reviewing license text and dataset attributions now, should have a decision by 16:00 PT. Amber may need a small attribution text change in the manifest.

Sam: Nova-instruct causing an embeddings shape mismatch in our dedupe pipeline after quantization test. Quick repro command I used:
```
python infra/cli/run_infer.py --model nova-instruct --batch 8 --max-tokens 1024 --embedding-dim 1536
```
Working on a patch to the preprocessor to normalize shapes.

Lee: Heads-up: dedupe jobs are also hitting transient storage mounts (infra-567). Eng-infra is investigating; they reported node reboots earlier which might explain failures.

canary-bot: Canary run started for release group 'openmodels-staging' at 2024-11-22T10:12:34Z (id: canary-789). Watching latency and error-rate.

Marta: Action items for gating: (1) @vikram finish kernel PR + smoke perf test; (2) @sam follow up with @eng-infra on infra-567 and share ETA; (3) @olivia-legal sign off amber7b or provide required manifest text; (4) @jess update manifest and open CR for the attribution change. If all clear, we plan staging->dedicated roll tomorrow morning.

Vikram: +1 from perf side if infra stabilizes. Note: zephyr-3b profile currently uses int8 kernels; switching to int4 will require re-running our eval harness.

Sam: Pinged eng-infra, they said ETA ~2 hours to remediate mounts and a node firmware rollback. I'll post updates in #eng-infra.

Jess: Manifest update in progress. Will open CR once I include the small attribution text and add the short test plan.

Olivia-Legal: Amber7b is cleared for hosted with the following attribution wording approved: "Dataset: AmberCC BY-SA 4.0 — attribution required, see manifest 'attribution' field." Sharing the text here so it can be copy/pasted.

Marta: Excellent — that removes the legal blocker. Biggest remaining risk is infra flakiness. If infra is green before 14:00 PT we'll proceed with the rollout window. This thread will be our single source for the go/no-go decision.

Lee: Eng-infra updated the incident — they expect mount patch deployed in ~35m. I'll update the SRE channel and post back here when resolved.

Vikram: Also flagging: if we change quantization knobs for zephyr, we should tag a build with the quant profile and run the stability eval on the long-context benchmark (ticket PERF-222).

Jess: CR opened: https://git.redwood/platform/changes/789 — includes manifest change + test plan (smoke inference + attribution check). Please review.

Marta: Thanks all. I'll update the checklist doc and ping product for a release-note blurb once CR is approved. :thumbsup:

Lee: infra-567 marked RESOLVED at 1729954880 — storage mounts stable, canary still green per canary-bot.

Marta: Great — with legal sign-off, perf PR in flight, infra resolved, and CR opened, I'm calling this green for staging->dedicated tomorrow morning unless new blockers appear. Closing action: owners post final confirmation in this thread when they've merged/closed their items.

Vikram: Merged perf fix at 1729954940.

Sam: Patch for the embedding preprocessor pushed to branch, will open PR in 15m.

Jess: CR merged at 1729954980 — manifest updated with approved attribution.

Olivia-Legal: Noted. Thanks everyone.

Marta: Perfect — thanks team. I'll update the milestone and move this item to 'staged' in the launch board.
